quality.basis: 崩溃差分（LeakSanitizer，fuzz harness 输入）；用确定性短读代替竞态，标准答案据 exploit 构造

ground_truth_evidence: category 5: the dataset's own trigger (newplatform_bundles/conversion/c5/gt/libsass/vulnerability_WF_LLM_5/import.scss; adapted: exploit.sh imports a file whose size it races to change (a short read); the deterministic equivalent imports a sysfs attribute (`/sys/devices/system/cpu/possible`) whose stat size (one page) exceeds its content, so fread() always returns fewer bytes than stat() reported - the same short-read path, with no race. The exploit's own input alone does not leak (it needs the race); this imports a file that short-reads every time.)

review.note: a background loop truncates trigger.scss while data_context_fuzzer @imports it, so a short read leaks the buffer; the leak needs that race (verify_exploit.py: exploit.sh leaks the vulnerable build, its 23-byte input alone does not)

category5.design: The injected code drops `free(contents); fclose(fd);` when fread() returns fewer bytes than stat() reported (a short read), leaking the buffer. The exploit raced a background truncation to cause the short read, which a single-input PoV cannot reproduce reliably; instead the PoV imports a sysfs pseudo-file whose reported size (4096) always exceeds its few bytes of content, so every run short-reads and the vulnerable build leaks (LeakSanitizer, frame in read_file) while the secure build frees. LeakSanitizer is on (leak task).
